newsitem.title: GERMANY: Siemens sees no better results in 1996/97.
newsitem.headline: Siemens sees no better results in 1996/97.

text.p: German electronics and engineering conglomerate Siemens AG said on Wednesday it expected no improvement in its results in the 1996/97 business year.

The company reported that group profit after taxes in 1995/96 was 2.49 billion marks ($1.6 billion) , up 20 percent from the previous year, before inclusion of a 496 million mark extroardinary profit from the sale of a printer division. ($ = 1.522 German Marks)
Siemens sees no better results in 1996/97
"After two years of healthy expansion and a more than 50 percent increase in earnings excluding extraordinary gains, Siemens anticipates moderated growth this year," the company said in a statement.
"In view of declining earnings, notably in the components segment, as well as restructuring measures in the medical engineering group, net income is not expected to grow in fiscal 1997," it added.
Commenting on the 1995/96 results, Siemens said, "Continuing buoyant developments abroad more than compensated for stagnating domestic business."
Siemens worldwide workforce grew to 379,000 as of September 30 from 373,000 a year earlier as the company added more jobs outside Germany than it cut domestically.
